title: The punctured strictly local curve has DVR branches
statement:
Let $R$ be a reduced excellent one-dimensional
strictly henselian
local ring with algebraically closed residue field of
characteristic $p>0$. Its punctured spectrum is a finite
disjoint union of spectra of fraction fields of excellent
strictly henselian DVRs with that same residue field.
These fields are the factors obtained from the
branch algebra.

proof.text: Write $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and use [def-exc-local-curve-branches] to set $A_a=R/\mathfrak p_a$, $K_a=\operatorname{Frac}(A_a)$, and $N_a=\overline{A_a}^{K_a}$, so that $B(R)=\prod_aN_a$. Excellence includes Noetherianity by [def-exc-excellent-ring], and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] makes the set of indices finite. Each $A_a$ is a local domain of dimension exactly one: its primes correspond to primes of $R$ containing $\mathfrak p_a$, and only $\mathfrak p_a$ and $\mathfrak m$ can occur, since an intermediate prime would give a chain of length two. They are distinct, since a minimal maximal ideal in a local ring would be its only prime and force dimension zero. For an ideal $J$ of $A_a$, its preimage $I$ in $R$ is finitely generated by Noetherianity; the images of generators of $I$ generate $J$. Thus the quotient is Noetherian. Thus $A_a$ is in particular semilocal.

source.place: Tag 0C3R, lemma-pre-pre-delta-invariant; elementary dimension-one quotient argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata] to R. The Nagata condition [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] makes each minimal-prime quotient A_a N-2. Taking its own fraction field in [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] gives Module.Finite A_a N_a; transitivity of finite modules makes N_a finite over R. This is the finiteness needed for the henselian decomposition.

source.place: Tag 07QV, lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata; Algebra Definitions 032R and 032F; this proves directly the finiteness used in Tag 0C3S

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-semilocal-dim-one-normalization] to each $A_a$: step 1 supplies a semilocal Noetherian domain of dimension one, and $N_a$ is its integral closure in precisely its own fraction field. Its conclusion gives that $N_a$ is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of dimension one, semilocal, and that its fraction field is $K_a$. No henselianity or smoothness hypothesis is needed for this application.

source.place: Tag 09N2, lemma-semi-local-dimension-one-conductor, first assertion, as stated by the cited existing normalization node

proof.text: The ring $R$ is henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and each $N_a$ is finite over $R$ by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] to $R\to N_a$. Since $N_a$ is a nonzero domain, its decomposition into nonzero local rings has exactly one factor: two factors would give a coordinate idempotent different from $0,1$, contrary to $e(e-1)=0$ in a domain; zero factors would give the zero ring. Consequently $N_a$ itself is henselian local, its maximal ideal contracts to $\mathfrak m$, and its residue field $k_a$ is a finite extension of $k$. This extension is the given copy of $k$: each $x\in k_a$ has a minimal polynomial over $k$, and algebraic closedness of $k$ makes every irreducible such polynomial linear. Thus $k\to k_a$ is an isomorphism. In particular $k_a$ is separably closed, so $N_a$ is strictly henselian. Its residue characteristic is the same $p$.

source.place: Tag 04GH, lemma-finite-over-henselian, parts (1),(2); elementary domain-idempotent and algebraically closed field arguments

proof.text: By steps 3 and 4, N_a is a local Dedekind domain of Krull dimension exactly one. It is not a field, since a field has dimension zero. Mathlib IsDiscreteValuationRing.TFAE, implication from IsDedekindDomain to IsDiscreteValuationRing in a nonfield local domain, therefore gives the required DVR structure directly. This replaces the regular-local-ring declaration attached to lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr.

Each $N_a$ is a finite type $R$-algebra: an algebra containing its finite module-generating family contains every $R$-linear combination of the family, hence all of $N_a$. This is the finite type condition of [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Apply [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] with $A=N_a$ and $S=\{1\}$ to conclude that each $N_a$ is excellent.

Choose f from [lem-exc-local-curve-principal-total-fractions]. Its radical is the maximal ideal, so D(f) is exactly the punctured spectrum, and its localization is the total ring of fractions Q(R). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] to obtain an R-algebra equivalence Q(R) with the product of the minimal-prime localizations. The canonical maps from those localizations to their residue fields are bijective by that theorem. Each residue field is a fraction field of R/p_a, so the unique fraction-field algebra equivalence identifies it with K_a. Compose these algebra equivalences and reindex by the canonical equivalence between minimal prime spectra and branch ideals. The resulting equivalence R_f with the product of K_a commutes with the R-algebra maps. Step 3 identifies K_a as a fraction field of N_a.

source.place: Tag 0C3R, lemma-pre-pre-delta-invariant, reduced case; explicit comparison with the branch algebra

proof.text: Use Mathlib sigmaSpec and its finite-index isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], followed by Spec of the R-algebra equivalence in step 7. The resulting map from the coproduct to Spec R_f is an isomorphism. Its composite with Spec R_f to Spec R is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] whose range is D(f). The open immersion D(f) to Spec R has the same range, so isoOfRangeEq gives the required scheme isomorphism. Check the equality over Spec R on every coprojection, using the projection formula for sigmaSpec and commutation of the algebra equivalence with the structure maps.

source.place: Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; finite-product spectrum identification from the cited Mathlib leaf
